ImageDescription.value:
This photograph accompanied an article titled Baseball History which summarized the 1918 baseball season of the Upper Arlington team. Baseball games were held at the Upper Arlington Ball Park on Thompson Field, which was located north of King Avenue, east of Bedford Road, and south of Tremont Road. Games were played during the summer with practices held on Tuesday evenings and games played on Saturday afternoons. Several people are named in the photograph.

Top Row: George S. Hershey ("George Washington"); Ed Nace; Frank P. Rogers ("Mexican"); Paul G. Spence ("Sure-Shot"); King Gibson Thompson ("Two-Bits"); Orr S. Zimmerman ("Home-Run"); Carey Clayton Hoel ("Smiles"); William F. Kern ("Has-Been"); Henry Miller ("Baldy"); John Weller Wuichet ("Pat"); Manager, Evan Lawrence Mahaffey.
Middle Row: Herman Rolf ("Jockey"); Frank J. Bornhauser ("Shorty"); Dr. Earl Ryan ("Doc" or "Curly"); Evan J. Crane ("Owl"); J. J. Morgan ("Pierpont"); Captain, George Woodford Thomas ("Goat"), Herbert Sherwood Warwick ("Runt").
Bottom Row: batboys, mascots, and water carriers.

ImageDescription.value: Common sole (Solea solea), Arrábida Natural Park, Portugal. The common sole is a species of flatfish in the family Soleidae. It lives on the sandy or muddy seabed of the northern Atlantic and the Mediterranean Sea where it often semi-immerses itself in the substrate as seen on the image. The small eyes are close to each other on the right side of the body. This gives the fish the possibility of lurking half-buried in the sand for passing prey. The common sole, just like all other flatfishes, hatches as an "ordinary" fish with one eye on each side of the body. The young metamorphose to flatfish when they are about one centimeter long. The upper side is greyish-brown and the underside is white. It grows to a maximum length of about 70 cm (28 in) although this exemplar was about 30 cm (12 in) long. The species is prized as a food fish, being caught mostly by trawling on the seabed.

ImageDescription.value: Spanning over 101,000 hectares, the Serra da Estrela Natural Park is the largest natural conservation area in Portugal. The park is located in the country’s largest mountain range, the Serra da Estrela, and contains the highest spot in Portugal. This Copernicus Sentinel-2 image from 23 April 2025 shows the Estrela Mountain upper Plateau and upper Zêzere River. This part of the park is designated as a biogenetic reserve and Natura 2000 site. It comprises the upper mountain and plateau, the Candeeira valley, and parts of the Zêzere river valley, which is a transition zone between the temperate and Mediterranean macrobioclimate. The Copernicus Sentinel satellites deliver free and open data useful for monitoring important ecosystems around the world. This information informs strategies to ensure that their unique characteristics and wildlife are better preserved.

ImageDescription.value:
General Context: Infrared photograph taken at Ilha do Cardoso State Park, documenting the flooding of mangrove areas due to sea-level rise. Because of the infrared technique, the colours are unnatural. The composition is minimalist, divided almost exactly in half between the sky and the water.
  • Foreground (Bottom half of the image): Occupies the entire lower half of the photo. It consists of a flat, smooth, and reflective surface of very shallow water over sand. The colour of this area is a uniform salmon-pink or light orange shade. On the left side, there is the elongated, inverted reflection of a tree, pointing towards the bottom edge of the image.
  • Middle Ground (The Centre and Horizon Line):A straight, horizontal line divides the image in half. On the left side, off-centre, a single dead tree trunk rises directly from the water. The tree is leafless, its colour is reddish-brown, and its upper branches form a 'Y' shape. Along the entire horizon line, separating the water from the sky, there is a narrow, white, blurred band, resembling distant breaking waves or low mist.
  • Background (Top half of the image): Occupies the upper half. It is composed entirely of the sky. The colour is a solid, continuous teal (cyan-blue), which slightly darkens at the top corners. There are small, thin white cloud formations concentrated just above the horizon line, and a solitary, wispy cloud in the upper right corner.
